explanation: Keep ASCII letters and digits, normalize letters to lowercase, and compare the filtered sequence with its reverse.
timeComplexity: O(n) time for n characters. Filtering, normalizing, and comparing the reversal each scan at most n characters.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary space. The filtered sequence and reversal contain at most n characters each.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 Java algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Filtering removes only the characters the contract says to ignore, and lowercasing normalizes the remaining ASCII letters. A sequence is a palindrome exactly when it equals its reversal, so comparing the filtered sequence with its reverse implements the stated rule.
walkthrough: For "No lemon, no melon!", filtering and lowercasing gives "nolemonnomelon". Reading it backward gives the same sequence, so return true.
edgeCases: Only ASCII letters and digits are retained.
A string with no retained characters is a palindrome.
Punctuation and spaces do not contribute mirrored positions.
